It does NOT reopen any v1.0 design decision Ramalingam already adjudicated.\n\n---\n\n## \u00a7 0.0c \u2014 Product-relevance audit of replay guarantees (NEW v0.7 W6-15)\n\nWalk #6 Item 15 raised the architectural concern that v0.6's replay infrastructure was approaching dominance over the optimization core itself. v0.7 responds with an explicit audit, declaring product-criticality per replay surface:\n\n| Surface | Product-criticality | Rationale | If product priorities shift |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| **TIER-1 byte-equal Pareto fronts** | **PRODUCT-CRITICAL** | Cache correctness depends on it: the same `EnvironmentFingerprint` MUST produce the same outputs, otherwise cache returns stale data. Without TIER-1, the cache becomes a correctness liability rather than an optimization | Removal would require redesigning the cache contract; deferred-evaluation pattern instead |\n| **TIER-2 structurally-equivalent (1e-9 + dominance + cardinality)** | **PRODUCT-CRITICAL** | Used in CI regression detection across BLAS/platform drift. Without TIER-2, a single CI tuple change forces full pipeline re-validation manually | Replaced with snapshot-comparison CI; lower confidence in cross-platform drift detection |\n| **TIER-3 statistically-equivalent (paired Wilcoxon hypervolume)** | **RESEARCH/DEBUG** | Only used when CI tuples themselves change (NumPy major version, new BLAS variant). Deferred to B-NEW-W. Operator-facing usefulness limited until hypervolume tooling exists | Drop entirely; cross-CI-tuple changes get explicit operator review instead |\n| **Deterministic tie-break (\u00a7 0.7.1)** | **PRODUCT-CRITICAL** | Required by TIER-1; without it, byte-equal Pareto fronts are impossible | (Removing would remove TIER-1 with it) |\n| **`master_seed` config field** | **PRODUCT-CRITICAL** | Reproducibility starting point; operator-controllable | (Cannot remove without removing replay) |\n| **`tiebreak_fingerprint` precompute** | **PRODUCT-CRITICAL** | Performance: avoids O(N\u00b2) hash work per generation | (Could revert to per-sort hashing, accept perf cost) |\n| **`per_topology_telemetry`, `longest_generation_seconds`, `skipped_*` counters** | **OPERATIONAL** | Diagnostic value for production tuning; not correctness | Verbosity knob already gates these |\n| **`resolved_objective_count`, `nsga2_objective_count_warning`** | **OPERATIONAL** | Signals NSGA-II 3-objective limitation; informs B-NEW-V5 migration | Drop if NSGA-III lands first |\n\n**Net product surface**: 6 PRODUCT-CRITICAL, 2 OPERATIONAL, 1 RESEARCH/DEBUG. v1 ships all surfaces; operators can selectively quiet OPERATIONAL via verbosity. RESEARCH/DEBUG TIER-3 is deferred \u2014 landing it post-v1 is fine.\n\nThe reviewer's Item 15 concern was that replay infrastructure was overshadowing optimization. The audit shows: of 9 listed replay surfaces, 6 are genuinely product-critical (cache correctness depends on them), 2 are operational, 1 is research/debug. Emit `RefinedCandidate`s carrying 3 capability flags + tiebreak_fingerprint + source_topology_candidate_signature\n\n**Key invariants for builders**:\n- Inv 26: `_resolve_input_artifact` is the only path\n- Inv 27: Per-topology wall-clock breach raises\n- Inv 28: Skip cap = `max(1, int(pop_size * config.evaluator_skip_cap_fraction))`\n- Inv 29: PRNG determinism + TIER-1/2/3 replay equivalence (\u00a7 0.7 + \u00a7 0.7.2)\n- Plus carried v1.0 Inv 1-25 (in main v0.4 spec carry section)\n\n**v1 capability flag equality** (\u00a7 0.3.1): `placement_safe == geometry_materialized AND requires_transform_resolution == NOT geometry_materialized`. Constructed via `RefinedCandidate.from_operator_class(operator, ...)` helper.\n\n**v1 PRODUCT-CRITICAL surfaces** (\u00a7 0.0c): TIER-1 byte-equal, TIER-2 structural, deterministic tie-break, master_seed, tiebreak_fingerprint precompute, capability flags.\n\nIf anything above is unclear, the full spec body is the source of truth; Skip that one candidate; continue the generation.\n2. **Systemic failure** (evaluator raises any other exception type): the evaluator itself is broken (e.g., C14 KB lookup failed, model file missing). Halt the topology, raise `EvaluatorContractError` wrapping the underlying cause.\n3. **Per-candidate flood** (>25% of population fails per-candidate in one generation): treat as systemic regardless of declared error type. Indicates the evaluator's contract is mismatched with C11b's population, not isolated bad candidates.\n\n**v0.4 mechanism** (Phase 1 per-generation):\n\n```python\ndef _evaluate_population(\n    population: tuple[RefinedCandidate, ...],\n    evaluator: EvaluatorProtocol,\n    config: LocalRefinementConfig,\n) -> tuple[tuple[RefinedCandidate, ...], int]:\n    \"\"\"Returns (evaluated_population, skipped_count).\n\n    Per Inv 28: skip count cap is\n    ``max(1, int(pop_size * config.evaluator_skip_cap_fraction))``\n    (default 0.25 \u2192 25 of 100). Cache lookup uses the full fingerprint including this field; runs under version=1 cannot collide with runs under version=2 even if everything else (master_seed, c11b_version, NumPy version) is identical.\n   883\t\n   884\t**Why this is high severity (despite the small spec change)**: at v0.6 a contributor amending C7 or C11a to change `CANONICAL_FP_PRECISION` (currently 6, in `buildemup/utilities/canonical.py`) for a legitimate reason would NOT bump `c11b_version` (because C11b code didn't change). This is a deliberate tradeoff: tolerate edge-case evaluator brittleness, hard-fail systemic mis-wiring.\n\n---\n\n## \u00a7 0.7 \u2014 PRNG seed derivation (D-PR-1, D-PR-2)\n\n**Rationale**: v1.0 spec mentions \"per-topology rng seed\" but doesn't specify derivation. Standard practice: set seeds across all RNGs (Python's random, NumPy's RandomState/Generator, any backend like PyTorch) from a single master seed via a deterministic mixing function. Without specification, two runs of the same nominal config could produce different streams if NumPy's RNG defaults change.\n\n**v0.4 mechanism**:\n\n```python\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass LocalRefinementConfig:\n    ...  # carried v1.0\n    master_seed: int = field(                     # NEW v0.4\n        default=0xC11B5EED,                       # deliberately recognizable\n        metadata={\"cache_relevant\": True},        # affects output; cached separately\n    )\n\ndef derive_per_topology_seed(\n    master_seed: int,\n    topology_index: int,\n    topology_signature: str,\n) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Pure deterministic derivation per Inv 29.\n\n    Uses SHA256 over the canonical concatenation. Truncated to 32 bits\n    so NumPy's SeedSequence accepts it (any int up to 2^32 is fine;\n    larger ints would also work but 32 bits keeps logs readable).\n    \"\"\"\n    payload = f\"{master_seed}|{topology_index}|{topology_signature}\"\n    h = hashlib.sha256(payload.encode(\"utf-8\")).digest()\n    return int.from_bytes(h[:4], byteorder=\"big\")\n\ndef _build_per_topology_rng(\n    config: LocalRefinementConfig,\n    topology_index: int,\n    topology_signature: str,\n) -> numpy.random.Generator:\n    \"\"\"Build per-topology PRNG via explicit SeedSequence for NumPy\n    version stability.\n\n    Rationale: numpy.random.default_rng(int) semantics have been stable\n    since NumPy 1.17, but NumPy's recommended practice is to construct\n    via SeedSequence explicitly to make the intent unambiguous and to\n    enable reproducible spawning in future parallel implementations\n    (B-NEW-Z deterministic-parallel-NSGA-II).\n    \"\"\"\n    seed = derive_per_topology_seed(\n        config.master_seed, topology_index, topology_signature,\n    )\n    seed_seq = numpy.random.SeedSequence(seed)\n    return numpy.random.default_rng(seed_seq)\n```\n\n**Invariant 29 (NEW v0.4, REVISED v0.5 Item 11, REVISED v0.6 W5-1 + W5-10)**: PRNG seed derivation is pure-deterministic. Replay equivalence is specified as three explicit tiers (NEW v0.6 W5-1 nomenclature):\n\n**TIER-1 \u2014 Byte-equal Pareto fronts**. Holds as a CONJUNCTION of:\n  - same `master_seed`, `topology_index`, `topology_signature`\n  - same CI-validated environment tuple (numpy_version, BLAS, platform_machine, platform_system, `c11b_version`) per `EnvironmentFingerprint`\n  - deterministic tie-break rule applied (per \u00a7 0.7.1 below)\n\nReplay tests asserting TIER-1 require all three conditions; missing any one drops to TIER-2.\n\n**TIER-2 \u2014 Structurally-equivalent Pareto fronts**. Holds when the seed/env/tie-break conjunction is partial (e.g., different BLAS but same algorithm + seed). Asserted as a CONJUNCTION of three conditions (v0.6 W5-10 strengthening \u2014 previously v0.5 was numeric-only):\n  - **Same Pareto rank cardinality per front**: `len(front_k_runA) == len(front_k_runB)` for each rank `k`\n  - **Same dominance relations across the front**: for every pair `(a, b)` in the union of both runs' candidates, `a dominates b in run A iff a dominates b in run B`\n  - **Numeric tolerance**: `1e-9` absolute on objective values; same objective-vector mapping (same keys, same ordering)\n\nThe conjunction prevents cumulative floating-point drift over many generations from being silently masked as \"structurally equivalent\" while the actual dominance topology has shifted (v0.5 numeric-only tolerance had this hole).\n\n**TIER-3 \u2014 Statistically-equivalent Pareto fronts**. Holds across CI-incompatible environments (cross-platform, different NumPy major version). Asserted via paired hypervolume comparison (Wilcoxon signed-rank, p > 0.05) over a benchmark population. **Deferred to B-NEW-W (C11b hypervolume diversity metric)** \u2014 requires hypervolume computation infrastructure not present at v1. TIER-3 tests will land alongside B-NEW-W.\n\n`topology_signature`: Reuse C11a's `derive_canonical_signature(input_artifact)` output (16-hex SHA256 prefix). For multi-floor wrappers this would aggregate per-floor signatures; v1 doesn't see multi-floor inputs (per D-MF-1), so the signature is the single-floor structural hash.\n\n**Per-replay assertion**: Phase 0 captures `master_seed` into `EnvironmentFingerprint`. TIER-1 tests assert byte-equality. TIER-2 tests assert the three-condition conjunction. TIER-3 tests are deferred per B-NEW-W trigger.\n\n### \u00a7 0.7.1 \u2014 Deterministic tie-break rule (NEW v0.5 Item 6, REVISED v0.6 W5-12)\n\nNSGA-II's survival selection picks individuals first by Pareto rank, then by crowding distance descending. When candidates tie on BOTH (e.g., extreme points get `crowding_distance = +inf` and there are multiple), the algorithm's behavior depends on implementation. v0.5 specified the rule explicitly; v0.6 W5-12 optimizes layer 2 from per-sort `canonical_serialize` to a precomputed integer fingerprint.\n\n**Rule**: Within an equivalence class of (rank, crowding_distance) ties, candidates are ordered by lex-ASC composite key:\n```python\ndef _tiebreak_key(candidate: RefinedCandidate, candidate_index: int) -> tuple:\n    \"\"\"Lex-ASC tie-break for NSGA-II survivor selection per Inv 29.\n\n    Composite key:\n      1. topology_signature (deterministic from source artifact)\n      2. tiebreak_fingerprint (precomputed 64-bit int per v0.6 W5-12;\n         was canonical_serialize hash per v0.5, now precomputed once\n         at RefinedCandidate.__post_init__ to avoid O(N\u00b2) hash work)\n      3. candidate_index (insertion order in the current population)\n< truncated lines 819-832 >\n        candidate.source_topology_candidate_signature,  # exposed via \u00a7 2.1\n        candidate.tiebreak_fingerprint,                  # precomputed v0.6 W5-12\n        candidate_index,\n    )\n```\n\n**`tiebreak_fingerprint` derivation** (REVISED v0.7 W6-3 for version safety; computed once at `RefinedCandidate.__post_init__`):\n\n```python\n# Module-level constant in c11b/tiebreak.py (NEW v0.7 W6-3):\nTIEBREAK_FINGERPRINT_SCHEMA_VERSION: Final[int] = 1\n\"\"\"Bump rule (must be documented in commit message):\n  - Increment when canonical_serialize semantics change in a way that\n    affects RefinedParameters serialization (float precision change,\n    field ordering change, normalization rule change, etc.).\n  - Increment when the derivation function below changes (different\n    hash, different byte count, different mixing).\n  - Do NOT increment for non-affecting changes elsewhere in the codebase.\n\nThe version is captured into `EnvironmentFingerprint.tiebreak_fingerprint_schema_version: int`\nso cache keys observe it directly. A cache entry computed under\nversion=1 deserializes-miss under version=2.\n\"\"\"\n\ndef _compute_tiebreak_fingerprint(refined_parameters: RefinedParameters) -> int:\n    \"\"\"64-bit big-endian int from first 8 bytes of\n    sha256(VERSION + canonical_serialize(refined_parameters)).\n\n    v0.7 W6-3 change: the schema version is prepended to the payload\n    before hashing. This makes the fingerprint explicitly dependent on\n    the version, so changing canonical_serialize semantics WITHOUT\n    bumping the version produces detectably different fingerprints\n    (which then cache-miss correctly via EnvironmentFingerprint).\n\n    Without this version-anchor (v0.6 behavior), a silent\n    canonical_serialize change in any upstream component (e.g., C7\n    changing float precision) would produce different fingerprints\n    AT THE SAME c11b_version, silently corrupting cache integrity.\n    \"\"\"\n    versioned_payload = (\n        f\"{TIEBREAK_FINGERPRINT_SCHEMA_VERSION}|\"\n        + canonical_serialize(refined_parameters)\n    ).encode(\"utf-8\")\n    return int.from_bytes(\n        hashlib.sha256(versioned_payload).digest()[:8],\n        byteorder=\"big\",\n    )\n```\n\n**Cache-key composition (NEW v0.7 W6-3)**: `EnvironmentFingerprint` gains a new field `tiebreak_fingerprint_schema_version: int` that captures `TIEBREAK_FINGERPRINT_SCHEMA_VERSION` at run time. Cache lookup uses the full fingerprint including this field; runs under version=1 cannot collide with runs under version=2 even if everything else (master_seed, c11b_version, NumPy version) is identical.\n\n**Why this is high severity (despite the small spec change)**: at v0.6 a contributor amending C7 or C11a to change `CANONICAL_FP_PRECISION` (currently 6, in `buildemup/utilities/canonical.py`) for a legitimate reason would NOT bump `c11b_version` (because C11b code didn't change). All existing C11b cache entries would silently produce different `tiebreak_fingerprint` values, leading to wrong-keyed cache entries (same key, different content). This is a stealth correctness bug that the v0.6 spec hadn't surfaced. The W6-3 patch is the minimum-cost fix.\n\n**Applied at**: NSGA-II survivor selection (after crowding-distance assignment) and Pareto-front membership assignment when multiple candidates have identical objective vectors.\n\n**Test discipline**: 1 dedicated test asserts that two populations with intentionally tied candidates produce identical survivor sets across runs (TIER-1 byte-equal). 1 dedicated test asserts that swapping `candidate_index` (i.e., feeding the population in a different order) produces a DIFFERENT survivor set when ties exist \u2014 this proves the tie-break is reachable and order-sensitive, not silently disambiguated by upstream operations. 1 NEW v0.6 test asserts that `tiebreak_fingerprint` is deterministic across runs (same refined_parameters \u2192 same int) and that the sort uses the precomputed value rather than recomputing. 1 NEW v0.7 test asserts `tiebreak_fingerprint` includes `TIEBREAK_FINGERPRINT_SCHEMA_VERSION`: bumping the version while keeping `refined_parameters` identical produces a DIFFERENT fingerprint.\n\n**Cross-reference to B-NEW-Z (W6-12, candidate_index parallel-unsafety)**: layer 3 (`candidate_index`) is insertion-order-sensitive by design at v1. Single-threaded NSGA-II at v1 has stable insertion order; future parallel-NSGA-II (B-NEW-Z) must replace `candidate_index` with a deterministic order-invariant fallback (candidate UUID, structural hash, or ancestry lineage id). v0.7 does not change layer 3 at v1.\n\n### \u00a7 0.7.2 \u2014 TIER-3 minimum semantics (NEW v0.7 W6-4)\n\nv0.6 deferred TIER-3 (statistically-equivalent Pareto fronts) to B-NEW-W, with \"paired Wilcoxon hypervolume comparison\" as the only specified mechanism. v0.7 W6-4 freezes additional minimum semantics now so that future TIER-3 implementations cannot fragment:\n\n**Frozen at v0.7**:\n\n| Aspect | Frozen value | Rationale |\n|---|---|---|\n| Statistical test | Paired Wilcoxon signed-rank, two-tailed | Non-parametric, paired-sample appropriate for hypervolume comparison; standard in EA literature |\n| Minimum paired benchmark runs | 30 | Standard sample size for non-parametric tests; gives reasonable statistical power |\n| Significance threshold | p > 0.05 (i.e., NOT rejecting null = \"statistically equivalent\") | TIER-3 asserts EQUIVALENCE, not difference; failing to reject null is the equivalence claim |\n| Hypervolume normalization | Reference-point = (max observed in each objective across both compared runs) + 1.0 absolute offset | Reference-point sensitivity is a known hypervolume hazard; freezing the rule prevents drift across TIER-3 implementations |\n| Benchmark corpus version-anchor | `TIER3_BENCHMARK_CORPUS_VERSION: Final[int]` constant (to be defined in v1 release notes) | Different corpora produce different results; version-anchor required |\n| Confidence interval reporting | 95% CI on the median hypervolume difference, alongside p-value | Single p-value is fragile; CI shows effect size |\n\n**Deferred to B-NEW-W**:\n\n| Aspect | When defined |\n|---|---|\n| Hypervolume computation implementation | B-NEW-W spec arc |\n| Benchmark corpus contents | B-NEW-W spec arc |\n| TIER-3 test integration with CI matrix | B-237 + B-NEW-W intersection |\n\n**Why freeze minimum semantics without implementing**: v0.7 prevents the scenario where Walk #N+1 implements TIER-3 in one way, then Walk #N+2 reimplements it differently because the spec left too much room. Freezing what CAN be frozen now reduces future spec fragmentation risk.\n\n---\n\n## \u00a7 0.8 \u2014 Carried v1.0 sections (no v0.4 changes)\n\nAll of v1.0 \u00a7 0.6 (refinement bounds), \u00a7 0.7 (feasibility-aware init), \u00a7 0.8 (stagnation detection), \u00a7 0.9 (output ordering), \u00a7 0.10 (DominanceSorter scope), \u00a7 1 (Walk-resolved scope), \u00a7 13 (Complexity budget), \u00a7 14 (Freeze candidacy) carry forward verbatim. v0.4 does not amend them.\n\n---\n\n## \u00a7 1 \u2014 Walk-resolved scope (v0.4 additions)\n\n| Q / F / G | Resolution | Walk |\n|---|---|---|\n| (carried v0.1-v1.0) | \u2026 | \u2026 |\n| **G-S41-1 (D-MF-1)** | Multi-floor inputs rejected at v1 with `MultiFloorRefinementNotSupportedError`; B-C11B-MF files post-v1 work | v0.4 self-analysis |\n| **G-S41-2 (D-OC-1)** | C11b reads `MutationApplicationResult.output_candidate` when present; falls back to `source_candidate` for Tier A SHALLOW | v0.4 self-analysis |\n| **G-S41-3 (D-TO-1)** | `per_topology_wallclock_seconds=30.0` default; `PerTopologyTimeoutError` per-topology | v0.4 self-analysis |\n| **G-S41-4 (D-NSGA-1)** | `StubEvaluator.objectives` defaults to 3 (carries v0.3 LOCKED behavior); 2-objective mode added as configurable knob. Hypervolume-regression-based warning (the operationally correct semantics) is filed as backlog `B-C11B-HYPERVOLUME-WARN`.\n6. **Item 19** \u2014 v0.5 \u00a7 0.3.3 documented v1.0 \u2192 v1.1 migration but didn't define `C11B_VERSION` SemVer rules. v0.6 adds \u00a7 0.3.4 with explicit MAJOR/MINOR/PATCH semantics for cache-breaking, telemetry, replay, and invariant changes.\n\nThe 6 new backlog items (notable: Item 2 surfaces a recent peer-reviewed paper):\n\n- **B-C11B-DOERR-TIEBREAK** (Item 2 + Item 15) \u2014 Adopt Doerr et al. 2024 NSGA-II frequency-based tie-break (\"Speeding Up the NSGA-II With a Simple Tie-Breaking Rule\"). Proves NSGA-II can optimize benchmarks efficiently for many objectives. Addresses both v0.5 Items 2 + 15 (tie-break bias + 3-objective limitation) with a single proven literature remedy.\n- **B-C11B-CACHE-TIERS** (Item 4) \u2014 Cache-relevance tiering (OUTPUT_CRITICAL / REPLAY_CRITICAL / DIAGNOSTIC) instead of binary `cache_relevant: bool`.\n- **B-C11B-PROVENANCE-SPLIT** (Item 11) \u2014 Split `LocalRefinementProvenance` into ReplayProvenance + OperationalTelemetry + DiagnosticWarnings.\n- **B-C11A-MTC-SINGLETON** (Item 13) \u2014 C11a v1.6 amendment to expose `primary_application_result` as a singleton field; eliminates tuple-vs-singleton schema dishonesty.\n- **B-C11B-COMPLEXITY-BUDGET-V2** (Item 14) \u2014 Weighted complexity metric (invariants + cache-affecting fields + replay constraints + telemetry fields) alongside subsystem count.\n- **B-C11B-SPEC-SPLIT-V2** (Item 20) \u2014 Documentation split: C11b-Core-Optimization / C11b-Replay / C11b-Provenance / C11b-Failure-Policy.\n- **B-PIPELINE-CAPABILITY-NEGOTIATION** (Item 7, ROUTED TO ORCHESTRATOR) \u2014 Upstream capability flag so MF-incapable downstreams suppress MF generation. Operate on bare float vectors with\nexplicit lower/upper bounds; the C11b ``phase1`` orchestrator marshals\n``RefinedParameters`` \u2194 float vectors around these calls.\n\nBoth operators are pure-deterministic given the input + the passed\n``numpy.random.Generator``. The Generator is the per-topology PRNG\nbuilt via ``_build_per_topology_rng``.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport numpy as np\n\n\ndef sbx_crossover(\n    parent_a: tuple[float, ...],\n    parent_b: tuple[float, ...],\n    lower: tuple[float, ...],\n    upper: tuple[float, ...],\n    rng: np.random.Generator,\n    *,\n    eta_c: float = 20.0,\n    crossover_probability: float = 0.9,\n) -> tuple[tuple[float, ...], tuple[float, ...]]:\n    \"\"\"Simulated Binary Crossover. Returns (child_a, child_b).\n\n    With probability ``crossover_probability`` per gene, the child genes\n    are spread around the parents per the SBX distribution; otherwise\n    the genes are copied from the parents.\n\n    Bounds are enforced post-mix via clipping. ``eta_c`` controls the\n    distribution sharpness (higher = closer to parents).\n    \"\"\"\n    n = len(parent_a)\n    assert len(parent_b) == n == len(lower) == len(upper), (\n        \"SBX requires matched-length parents + bounds.\"\n    )\n    child_a = list(parent_a)\n    child_b = list(parent_b)\n    for i in range(n):\n        if rng.random() >= crossover_probability:\n            continue\n        if abs(parent_a[i] - parent_b[i]) < 1e-14:\n            continue\n        x1 = min(parent_a[i], parent_b[i])\n        x2 = max(parent_a[i], parent_b[i])\n        xl, xu = lower[i], upper[i]\n        if xu <= xl:\n            continue\n        rand = rng.random()\n        # SBX \u03b2 derivation.\n        beta = 1.0 + (2.0 * (x1 - xl) / (x2 - x1))\n        alpha = 2.0 - beta ** -(eta_c + 1.0)\n        if rand <= 1.0 / alpha:\n            betaq = (rand * alpha) ** (1.0 / (eta_c + 1.0))\n        else:\n            betaq = (1.0 / (2.0 - Returns the mutated vector.\n\n    ``mutation_probability`` defaults to ``1/n`` (Deb's standard).\n    ``eta_m`` controls perturbation magnitude (higher = closer to\n    parent).\n    \"\"\"\n    n = len(parent)\n    if mutation_probability is None:\n        mutation_probability = 1.0 / max(1, n)\n    out = list(parent)\n    for i in range(n):\n        if rng.random() >= mutation_probability:\n            continue\n        xl, xu = lower[i], upper[i]\n        if xu <= xl:\n            continue\n        y = out[i]\n        delta1 = (y - xl) / (xu - xl)\n        delta2 = (xu - y) / (xu - xl)\n        rand = rng.random()\n        mut_pow = 1.0 / (eta_m + 1.0)\n        if rand < 0.5:\n            xy = 1.0 - delta1\n            val = 2.0 * rand + (1.0 - 2.0 * rand) * (xy ** (eta_m + 1.0))\n            deltaq = val**mut_pow - 1.0\n        else:\n            xy = 1.0 - delta2\n            val = 2.0 * (1.0 - rand) + 2.0 * (rand - 0.5) * (xy ** (eta_m + 1.0))\n            deltaq = 1.0 - val**mut_pow\n        y = y + deltaq * (xu - xl)\n        out[i] = min(max(y, xl), xu)\n    return tuple(out)\n\n\n__all__ = [\n    \"sbx_crossover\",\n    \"polynomial_mutation\",\n]\n",

Operate on bare float vectors with\nexplicit lower/upper bounds; the C11b ``phase1`` orchestrator marshals\n``RefinedParameters`` \u2194 float vectors around these calls.\n\nBoth operators are pure-deterministic given the input + the passed\n``numpy.random.Generator``. The Generator is the per-topology PRNG\nbuilt via ``_build_per_topology_rng``.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport numpy as np\n\n\ndef sbx_crossover(\n    parent_a: tuple[float, ...],\n    parent_b: tuple[float, ...],\n    lower: tuple[float, ...],\n    upper: tuple[float, ...],\n    rng: np.random.Generator,\n    *,\n    eta_c: float = 20.0,\n    crossover_probability: float = 0.9,\n) -> tuple[tuple[float, ...], tuple[float, ...]]:\n    \"\"\"Simulated Binary Crossover. Returns (child_a, child_b).\n\n    With probability ``crossover_probability`` per gene, the child genes\n    are spread around the parents per the SBX distribution; otherwise\n    the genes are copied from the parents.\n\n    Bounds are enforced post-mix via clipping. ``eta_c`` controls the\n    distribution sharpness (higher = closer to parents).\n    \"\"\"\n    n = len(parent_a)\n    assert len(parent_b) == n == len(lower) == len(upper), (\n        \"SBX requires matched-length parents + bounds.\"\n    )\n    child_a = list(parent_a)\n    child_b = list(parent_b)\n    for i in range(n):\n        if rng.random() >= crossover_probability:\n            continue\n        if abs(parent_a[i] - parent_b[i]) < 1e-14:\n            continue\n        x1 = min(parent_a[i], parent_b[i])\n        x2 = max(parent_a[i], parent_b[i])\n        xl, xu = lower[i], upper[i]\n        if xu <= xl:\n            continue\n        rand = rng.random()\n        # SBX \u03b2 derivation.\n        beta = 1.0 + (2.0 * (x1 - xl) / (x2 - x1))\n        alpha = 2.0 - beta ** -(eta_c + 1.0)\n        if rand <= 1.0 / alpha:\n            betaq = (rand * alpha) ** (1.0 / (eta_c + 1.0))\n        else:\n            betaq = (1.0 / (2.0 - rand * alpha)) ** (1.0 / (eta_c + 1.0))\n        c1 = 0.5 * ((x1 + x2) - betaq * (x2 - x1))\n\n        beta = 1.0 + (2.0 * (xu - x2) / (x2 - x1))\n        alpha = 2.0 - beta ** -(eta_c + 1.0)\n        if rand <= 1.0 / alpha:\n            betaq = (rand * alpha) ** (1.0 / (eta_c + 1.0))\n        else:\n            betaq = (1.0 / (2.0 - rand * alpha)) ** (1.0 / (eta_c + 1.0))\n        c2 = 0.5 * ((x1 + x2) + betaq * (x2 - x1))\n\n        c1 = min(max(c1, xl), xu)\n        c2 = min(max(c2, xl), xu)\n        if rng.random() < 0.5:\n            child_a[i], child_b[i] = c2, c1\n        else:\n            child_a[i], child_b[i] = c1, c2\n    return tuple(child_a), tuple(child_b)\n\n\ndef polynomial_mutation(\n    parent: tuple[float, ...],\n    lower: tuple[float, ...],\n    upper: tuple[float, ...],\n    rng: np.random.Generator,\n    *,\n    eta_m: float = 20.0,\n    mutation_probability: float | None = None,\n) -> tuple[float, ...]:\n    \"\"\"Polynomial mutation. Returns the mutated vector.\n\n    ``mutation_probability`` defaults to ``1/n`` (Deb's standard).\n    ``eta_m`` controls perturbation magnitude (higher = closer to\n    parent).\n    \"\"\"\n    n = len(parent)\n    if mutation_probability is None:\n        mutation_probability = 1.0 / max(1, n)\n    out = list(parent)\n    for i in range(n):\n        if rng.random() >= mutation_probability:\n            continue\n        xl, xu = lower[i], upper[i]\n        if xu <= xl:\n            continue\n        y = out[i]\n        delta1 = (y - xl) / (xu - xl)\n        delta2 = (xu - y) / (xu - xl)\n        rand = rng.random()\n        mut_pow = 1.0 / (eta_m + 1.0)\n        if rand < 0.5:\n            xy = 1.0 - delta1\n            val = 2.0 * rand + (1.0 - 2.0 * rand) * (xy ** (eta_m + 1.0))\n            deltaq = val**mut_pow - 1.0\n        else:\n            xy = 1.0 - delta2\n            val = 2.0 * (1.0 - rand) + 2.0 * (rand - 0.5) * (xy ** (eta_m + 1.0))\n            deltaq = 1.0 - val**mut_pow\n        y = y + deltaq * (xu - xl)\n        out[i] = min(max(y, xl), xu)\n    return tuple(out)\n\n\n__all__ = [\n    \"sbx_crossover\",\n    \"polynomial_mutation\",\n]\n",

A purely combinatorial version of floor planning is the well-known Bin Packing problem, where items of different sizes must be packed into bins, each of a fixed capacity, in a way that minimizes the number of bins used. Bergman et al. [5] consider a variant called Bin Packing with Minimum Color Fragmentation, where each item is associated with a color. Capture `EnvironmentFingerprint` (reusing C11b's pattern; C12 adds its own version anchor `C12_VERSION: Final[str] = \"v0.1\"`).\n2. If `expected_environment_fingerprint` is provided and doesn't match, raise `EnvironmentFingerprintMismatchError`.\n3. For each single-floor input: assert `geometry_materialized is True AND placement_safe is True` per B-C12-MATERIALIZATION-CONTRACT. If `requires_transform_resolution is True` (Tier A SHALLOW input), invoke the **transform resolver** sub-step first (\u00a7 3.0a below) to materialize the pending geometry; then re-assert flags.\n\n### Phase 0a \u2014 Transform resolver (Tier A SHALLOW inputs)\n\nA C11b output with `capability_mode == \"PREDICATE_ONLY\"` carries a refined parameter vector but no materialized geometry. The transform resolver is the bridge: it takes the predicate verdict (which mutation operator the candidate represents) plus the refined dimensions and produces a candidate with `geometry_materialized = True`.\n\n**At v0.1, the resolver is a stub** that simply marks the candidate as materialized without doing real geometric transformation. Real per-operator resolvers are filed as `B-C12-TIER-A-RESOLVERS` (per-operator implementations for M1\u2013M5, M9a\u2013d). This stub is sufficient for v1 ship if all SFP inputs are Tier B or M0 (already materialized).\n\n### Phase 1 \u2014 Single-floor placement (SFP) per candidate\n\nFor each `RefinedCandidate` in `single_floor_inputs`:\n\n1. Resolve transforms if needed (Phase 0a).\n2. Build the room-list from `refined_parameters.room_dimensions`.\n3. Pull adjacency hints from `floor_room_brief` (e.g., kitchen-adjacent-to-dining).\n4. Invoke `placement_algorithm` (default: slicing-tree partition; see \u00a7 3.1).\n5. On algorithm success: emit `PlacedCandidate` with placed rooms + computed `shared_edges`.\n6. On algorithm failure under `enforcement_mode=STRICT`: raise `GeometricInfeasibilityError`.\n7. On failure under `WARN`: record a `FailureRecord` and continue.\n\n### Phase 2 \u2014 Multi-floor refinement absorption (MFRA)\n\nFor each `MultiFloorWetZonePlannedCandidate` in `multi_floor_inputs`:\n\n1. Decompose into per-floor sub-candidates.\n2. Run Phase 1 (SFP) on each floor independently.\n3. Run Phase 3 (VAV) on the resulting tuple of `PlacedCandidate`s.\n4. If VAV fails AND iteration count < `multi_floor_max_realign_iterations`: feed alignment-delta back as constraint hints, retry SFP on misaligned floors with column-position constraints, re-run VAV.\n5. On convergence: emit `MultiFloorPlacedCandidate`.\n6. On exhaustion: raise `VerticalAlignmentError` (STRICT) or record (WARN).\n\n### Phase 3 \u2014 Vertical alignment verification (VAV)\n\nGiven a tuple of `PlacedCandidate`s, one per floor:\n\n1. Identify alignment-relevant features per floor:\n   - Structural columns (from C7 Grid)\n   - Wet-zone stack centroids (from C10 wet-zone metadata)\n   - Staircase landing/run rectangles (currently from FloorRoomBrief; long-term backlog: dedicated stair planner)\n2. For each feature, compute the per-floor `(x_m, y_m)` position.\n3. For each adjacent floor pair `(N, N+1)`: compute deltas; flag any feature whose delta exceeds `vertical_alignment_tolerance_m`.\n4. Build `VerticalAlignmentReport`. If all three alignment categories pass, emit success; else record deltas for the MFRA retry loop.\n\n### Phase 4 \u2014 Provenance assembly\n\nMirrors C11b \u00a7 3 Phase 3:\n\n- Capture env fingerprint + master_seed + algorithm used per candidate\n- Per-candidate telemetry: wallclock time, retry count, algorithm path\n- Structured failure records (B-C11B-FAILURE-SCHEMA-V2 form \u2014 adopted from day one in C12)\n\n---\n\n## \u00a7 3.1 \u2014 Slicing k-d-tree placement algorithm (v1 default)\n\nPer Knecht & K\u00f6nig 2010, the slicing-tree approach to residential floor plans:\n\n1. Sort rooms by area, descending.\n2. Recursively bisect the envelope along the longer dimension.\n3. At each cut, place the largest remaining room aligned to the cut, with shorter-dim against the envelope wall.\n4. If the room doesn't fit the bisected region, backtrack to a different cut orientation.\n5. Repeat until all rooms placed or backtrack limit exhausted.\n\nThis is O(n log n) typical and O(n!) worst-case (full backtrack). For n \u2264 15 rooms (typical Indian residential) the worst case is tractable. Adjacency hints from C8 promote/demote candidate placements but don't override the area-first heuristic at v1.\n\n**Algorithm correctness at v1**: deterministic given `master_seed` (used only for tie-break on equal-area rooms), produces a valid placement OR fails cleanly. Does NOT guarantee optimality.\n\n---\n\n## \u00a7 4 \u2014 Invariants (v0.1 \u2014 will grow during walks)\n\n| # | Invariant | Mode |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Every `PlacedRoom` is fully contained within `(0, 0)` to `(envelope_width_m, envelope_depth_m)`. | RAISE |\n| 2 | No two `PlacedRoom`s on the same floor have overlapping interiors (shared edges allowed). | RAISE |\n| 3 | `PlacedRoom.width_m == RefinedParameters.room_dimensions[i].width_m` for the corresponding room_id (geometry preserves refinement). Tolerance: `0.0` at v1 in `strict` mode; \u22645% deviation allowed under `lenient_shrink`. | RAISE (STRICT) |\n| 4 | Capability-flag consistency at input: `geometry_materialized AND placement_safe` MUST be True (per B-C12-MATERIALIZATION-CONTRACT). | RAISE |\n| 5 | For multi-floor outputs: every alignment-relevant feature aligns within `vertical_alignment_tolerance_m` across adjacent floors. | RAISE |\n| 6 | `floor_index` is monotonically non-decreasing across the `per_floor` tuple in a `MultiFloorPlacedCandidate`. | RAISE |\n| 7 | Deterministic output: same input + same config + same env fingerprint \u2192 byte-equal `PlacedCandidate` tuple. | RAISE (replay tier) |\n| 8 | Every `PlacedCandidate.source_refined_candidate_signature` matches the input `RefinedCandidate.source_topology_candidate_signature` (one-to-one provenance trace). | RAISE |\n| 9 | `placement_algorithm_used` field is populated and matches one of the literal values in `PlacementConfig.placement_algorithm`. | RAISE |\n| 10 | `shared_edges` is computed deterministically from `placed_rooms` (function of geometry, not algorithm state). | RAISE |\n\n---\n\n## \u00a7 5 \u2014 Failure modes (v0.1 \u2014 will grow)\n\n```\nPlacementError (base)\n\u251c\u2500\u2500 PerCandidatePlacementError\n\u2502   \u251c\u2500\u2500 GeometricInfeasibilityError    (no valid placement; STRICT mode)\n\u2502   \u251c\u2500\u2500 CapabilityFlagInconsistencyError  (Inv 4 violation)\n\u2502   \u251c\u2500\u2500 PlacementAlgorithmTimeoutError (per-candidate budget exceeded)\n\u2502   \u2514\u2500\u2500 TransformResolverError         (Tier A stub failure)\n\u251c\u2500\u2500 PerMultiFloorPlacementError\n\u2502   \u251c\u2500\u2500 VerticalAlignmentError         (VAV failed; MFRA retries exhausted)\n\u2502   \u2514\u2500\u2500 MultiFloorDecompositionError   (per-floor input malformed)\n\u251c\u2500\u2500 BatchAllPlacementsFailedError      (WARN mode: every input failed)\n\u251c\u2500\u2500 EnvironmentFingerprintMismatchError (replay tier)\n\u2514\u2500\u2500 InvariantViolationError            (systemic)\n```\n\n---\n\n## \u00a7 6 \u2014 Test coverage targets (v0.1)\n\n- ~30 SFP-only tests: small-envelope placement, large-envelope placement, adjacency-hint honoring, backtrack-on-infeasible, area-sort tie-break determinism, lenient_shrink mode.\n- ~20 VAV tests: column-aligned passing, column-misaligned failing, wet-stack alignment, staircase alignment, mixed-feature alignment.\n- ~25 MFRA tests: 2-floor convergence after 1 retry, 2-floor exhaustion after max-retries, 3-floor cascade, repair-mode behaviour.\n- ~15 orchestrator tests: STRICT/WARN escalation, env fingerprint replay, batch-all-failed, structured failure records.\n- ~10 invariant tests: Inv 1-10 each with positive and negative cases.\n\nTarget ~100 tests at v1 LOCK (mirrors C11a v0.1 scope before its walks expanded coverage).\n\n---\n\n## \u00a7 7 \u2014 Open questions at v0.1 (resolve during Walks #2-#N)\n\n- **Q-1 (HIGH)**: Placement algorithm choice. Slicing k-d-tree (v1 default) is fast but suboptimal. Should v1 ship with CSP-backtrack fallback enabled by default, or only as opt-in? Literature suggests CSP (Regateiro et al. 2012) handles non-rectangular envelopes better.\n- **Q-2 (MEDIUM)**: Vertical alignment tolerance default. `0.0` is strict; `0.05 m` (50mm) is forgiving. Indian construction tolerances are typically \u00b110mm at the slab level. Reviewer-likely critique: 0.0 is unachievable in practice; 0.05 is the right v1 default.\n- **Q-3 (MEDIUM)**: Multi-floor refinement loop bound. `3` retries is a starting point. Should this scale with floor count, or stay flat?\n- **Q-4 (LOW)**: Determinism via `master_seed`. Slicing tree is deterministic without rng; only tie-break uses it. Is `master_seed` needed at v1 or can we defer it to a parallel-execution Q?\n- **Q-5 (HIGH)**: Adjacency hints from C8. At v1 they're soft (promote/demote candidate placements). Should they ever be HARD? E.g., bathroom-must-be-adjacent-to-bedroom is a hard architectural constraint in some cultures. **Q-5 risks scope-creep into KB rules \u2014 guard against.**\n- **Q-6 (MEDIUM)**: Non-rectangular envelopes (L-shaped plots, corner plots). At v0.1 we assume rectangular; real Indian residential plots are often irregular. Probably backlog for v2.\n- **Q-7 (LOW)**: Handoff contract to C13. `shared_edges` should be sufficient; verify with C13 spec stub.\n- **Q-8 (MEDIUM)**: Performance budget. `10s per single-floor candidate` is generous; `30s for multi-floor with retries` is conservative. Verify against Indian residential pop sizes (typical: 10-15 rooms per floor).\n- **Q-9 (HIGH)**: Repair mode under input infeasibility. STRICT vs LENIENT_SHRINK. The LENIENT mode is dangerous \u2014 it silently changes C11b's refined output, breaking the C11b \u2192 C12 contract that \"C11b chooses dims; C12 places them.\" If we offer it, must we also emit a `repair_delta` provenance field?\n- **Q-10 (MEDIUM)**: Cache key. Does C12 have its own cache (extending C11b's env tuple), or does C12 piggyback C11b's cache by treating placement as deterministic given the input candidate signature?\n- **Q-11 (LOW)**: Multi-floor refinement re-running C11b. Should MFRA re-invoke C11b NSGA-II per floor (the v1.1 LOCKED `B-C11B-MF` deferral path), or just run SFP-per-floor with no re-refinement? v0.1 assumes the latter (simpler); reviewer may push for the former.\n- **Q-12 (LOW)**: Capability-flag handling for `M8_MULTI_FLOOR` operator class. At C11b v1.1, M8 is rejected. If C12 absorbs MF inputs that came from M8 mutations, do we re-classify them as `M0_BASE` for downstream consumers, or keep the M8 lineage in provenance?\n\n**12 open questions at v0.1.** All resolvable through Walks #2-#N before LOCK.\n\n---\n\n## \u00a7 8 \u2014 Backlog at v0.1 (Rule 9 enumeration \u2014 to be expanded each walk)\n\n| ID | Description | Origin | Trigger | Effort |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| **B-C12-TIER-A-RESOLVERS** | Per-operator transform resolvers for M1\u2013M5, M9a\u2013d that turn predicate-only Tier A SHALLOW C11b outputs into materialized geometry.       "code": "# C12 \u2014 Multi-Floor Placement & Vertical Alignment Engine \u2014 SPEC v0.1 PROPOSED\n\n**Component**: 12 (canonical Track 3 numbering \u2014 consumes C11b RefinedCandidates and C10 MultiFloorWetZonePlannedCandidates; feeds C13 Door Placement)\n\n**Status**: v0.1 PROPOSED. **NOT LOCKED.** Walk #1 seed.\n\n**Authority**: S43 Walk #1 author's draft. PENDING Ramalingam adjudication.\n\n**Scope decision (locked at S42 close)**: **C12-Wide** \u2014 vertical alignment + single-floor geometric placement + multi-floor refinement absorption.\n\n**Authored**: S43 Walk #1, post-C11b v1.1 LOCKED.\n\n---\n\n## \u00a7 0 \u2014 Architectural notes\n\nC12 sits between C11b (Local NSGA-II Refinement) and C13 (Door Placement). Its job is **geometric realization**: take refined parameter vectors (room dimensions from C11b) or rejected multi-floor candidates (from C10 via C11b's MF-rejection path) and produce fully placed geometry \u2014 every room with absolute `(x, y, width, depth)` coordinates inside the envelope, every floor verified for embeddability, and multi-floor outputs verified for vertical alignment (columns, wet-stacks, staircases) across floors.\n\n**Pipeline position**:\n\n```\nC10 \u2192 C11a \u2192 C11b \u2500\u2500single-floor\u2500\u2500> C12 \u2192 C13 \u2192 C14\n                \u2502\n                \u2514\u2500\u2500multi-floor rejection\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2518\n                                            (C12 absorbs at v1)\n```\n\n**What C12 IS (the C12-Wide scope adopted at S42 close)**:\n\n- **Single-floor placement (SFP)**: turn each `RefinedCandidate.refined_parameters.room_dimensions` (room IDs + width/depth pairs) into placed rectangles inside the envelope. Verify geometric embeddability (no overlap, fully contained, adjacency hints from C8 honoured to the extent feasible).\n- **Vertical alignment verification (VAV)**: for multi-floor candidates, verify that structural columns, wet-zone stacks, and staircase landings/runs align across floors within tolerance. Emit per-floor placed geometry plus alignment metadata.\n- **Multi-floor refinement absorption (MFRA)**: gateway for `MultiFloorWetZonePlannedCandidate` inputs that C11b rejected via `MultiFloorRefinementNotSupportedError`. Per-floor SFP + VAV iteration loop, bounded retries.\n- **Capability-flag enforcement at consume time**: per B-C12-MATERIALIZATION-CONTRACT (filed during C11b walks), assert `placement_safe == True AND geometry_materialized == True` on every input `RefinedCandidate` before placement. Tier A SHALLOW candidates (PREDICATE_ONLY) MUST resolve their pending transforms before reaching C12 \u2014 that resolver step is C12's first action on Tier A input.\n\n**What C12 is NOT** (recurring scope-creep risks; surfaced now to anticipate Walk #2 critique):\n\n- **NOT scoring or evaluation.** C12 produces placed geometry; C14 scores it. A placement that is geometrically valid but architecturally poor (e.g., dark interior bedroom) is still emitted; quality judgement is C14's job.\n- **NOT door / window placement.** Once rooms are placed, C13 picks door positions on shared walls. C12 emits placed rectangles + shared-edge adjacency graph; that's all C13 needs.\n- **NOT NSGA-II.** C11b already ran multi-objective optimization on parameter vectors. C12's job is to *realize* the chosen parameters as geometry, not to re-search. If SFP can't place a given parameter vector, the candidate is rejected (or repaired under lenient mode per Q-9 below); no Pareto search re-runs.\n- **NOT a renderer.** Coordinates are produced; visual output is C16.\n- **NOT a structural engineer.** Column-alignment verification is geometric (do columns at floor N and floor N+1 share `(x, y)` within tolerance?). Load-path analysis is post-v1.\n- **NOT user-facing.** No explanation strings beyond provenance trace. Human-language reports are C14/C16.\n\n**Architectural divergence from VLSI literature** (raised at Walk #1, expect critique):\n\nVLSI floorplanning (sequence-pair, Q-sequence, simulated annealing per Tang & Wong 2001) is the canonical placement-algorithm literature. Those techniques assume *flexible* module shapes (sized rectangles with adjustable aspect ratios) and optimize for wirelength + area; they're solving a different problem.\n\nC12 takes the opposite assumption: room dimensions are **already fixed** by C11b's NSGA-II refinement. C12's job is not to optimize layout area \u2014 it's to *verify* whether the chosen dimensions admit a valid placement at all, and to produce one if so. This means C12's \"placement algorithm\" is much closer to a *feasibility checker with backtracking* than a continuous optimizer. The trade-off is reduced placement quality vs the literature, but tight coupling to C11b's chosen parameter vector (which is the point \u2014 C11b is where multi-objective trade-offs are made). **Q-1 surfaces the algorithm choice for Walk #2.**\n\n---\n\n## \u00a7 1 \u2014 Walk-resolved scope\n\n| Q | Resolution | Walk |\n|---|---|---|\n| (none) | v0.1 has no walk-resolved scope. First scope decisions land at Walk #2. | \u2014 |\n\n---\n\n## \u00a7 2 \u2014 Contract\n\n### \u00a7 2.1 \u2014 Top-level signature\n\n```python\ndef place_and_align(\n    *,\n    single_floor_inputs: tuple[RefinedCandidate, ...] = (),\n    multi_floor_inputs: tuple[MultiFloorWetZonePlannedCandidate, ...] = (),\n    grid: Grid,\n    plot_analysis: PlotAnalysis,\n    floor_room_brief: FloorRoomBrief,\n    config: PlacementConfig | None = None,\n    expected_environment_fingerprint: EnvironmentFingerprint | None = None,\n) -> PlacementBatchResult:\n    \"\"\"\n    C12 entry point. Accepts BOTH single-floor and multi-floor inputs;\n    routes each through the appropriate sub-engine (SFP / MFRA).\n\n    Returns PlacementBatchResult with:\n      - placed_candidates: tuple of single-floor placed outputs\n      - multi_floor_placed_candidates: tuple of MF placed outputs\n      - provenance: PlacementProvenance (env fingerprint + counters\n                   + per-input telemetry, mirroring C11b \u00a7 2.1 shape)\n      - failure_summaries: structured records, NOT strings\n                          (per B-C11B-FAILURE-SCHEMA-V2 from S42\n                           critique \u2014 C12 adopts the structured form\n                           from day one rather than carrying C11b's\n                           string-based debt forward)\n    \"\"\"\n```\n\n### \u00a7 2.2 \u2014 Schema additions\n\n```python\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass PlacedRoom:\n    \"\"\"One room placed at absolute coordinates inside the envelope.\"\"\"\n    room_id: str\n    x_m: float          # bottom-left corner, x coordinate (metres)\n    y_m: float          # bottom-left corner, y coordinate (metres)\n    width_m: float      # x-extent\n    depth_m: float      # y-extent\n    floor_index: int    # 0 = ground floor; 1 = first floor; etc.\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass SharedEdge:\n    \"\"\"Adjacency between two PlacedRoom instances; consumed by C13.\"\"\"\n    room_a_id: str\n    room_b_id: str\n    axis: Literal[\"vertical\", \"horizontal\"]   # of the shared edge\n    overlap_start_m: float                     # along the shared axis\n    overlap_end_m: float\n    overlap_length_m: float                    # convenience: end - start\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass PlacedCandidate:\n    \"\"\"One single-floor placed candidate. Inv 18+ from C11b's\n    'area-feasible by construction' is upgraded here to\n    'geometry-realized by construction'.\"\"\"\n    placed_rooms: tuple[PlacedRoom, ...]\n    shared_edges: tuple[SharedEdge, ...]\n    source_refined_candidate_signature: str    # provenance back to C11b\n    floor_index: int                            # 0 at v1 single-floor\n    envelope_width_m: float\n    envelope_depth_m: float\n    placement_algorithm_used: Literal[\"slicing_kd_tree\", \"csp_fallback\"]\n    # geometry-materialized flag from upstream RefinedCandidate; MUST be True.\n    geometry_materialized: bool = True\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass VerticalAlignmentReport:\n    \"\"\"Per-multi-floor candidate alignment audit.\"\"\"\n    columns_aligned: bool\n    wet_stacks_aligned: bool\n    staircases_aligned: bool\n    misalignment_deltas_m: tuple[tuple[str, float], ...]\n    # ^ list of (feature_id, x-or-y delta in metres) for failures\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass MultiFloorPlacedCandidate:\n    \"\"\"Multi-floor placed candidate after VAV passes.\"\"\"\n    per_floor: tuple[PlacedCandidate, ...]\n    alignment_report: VerticalAlignmentReport\n    source_multifloor_candidate_signature: str\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass PlacementBatchResult:\n    placed_candidates: tuple[PlacedCandidate, ...]\n    multi_floor_placed_candidates: tuple[MultiFloorPlacedCandidate, ...]\n    provenance: PlacementProvenance\n    failure_records: tuple[FailureRecord, ...]\n    # ^ structured per B-C11B-FAILURE-SCHEMA-V2 pattern\n```\n\n### \u00a7 2.3 \u2014 Configuration\n\n```python\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass PlacementConfig:\n    # \u2500\u2500 algorithm selection \u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\n    placement_algorithm: Literal[\n        \"slicing_kd_tree\",     # v1 default; fast, deterministic\n        \"csp_backtrack\",       # fallback when slicing fails\n    ] = \"slicing_kd_tree\"\n    use_csp_fallback_on_slicing_failure: bool = True\n\n    # \u2500\u2500 single-floor placement budgets \u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\n    placement_max_retries: int = 50\n    per_candidate_wallclock_seconds: float = 10.0\n\n    # \u2500\u2500 multi-floor alignment \u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\n    vertical_alignment_tolerance_m: float = 0.0      # Q-2 default\n    multi_floor_max_realign_iterations: int = 3      # Q-3 default\n\n    # \u2500\u2500 enforcement \u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\n    enforcement_mode: EnforcementMode = EnforcementMode.WARN\n    # ^ same shape as C11b (carried for consistency)\n\n    repair_mode: Literal[\"strict\", \"lenient_shrink\"] = \"strict\"\n    # ^ Q-9: what if C11b's chosen dims don't fit? STRICT rejects;\n    #   LENIENT_SHRINK tries to shrink dims by \u22645% before rejecting.\n\n    # \u2500\u2500 determinism \u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\n    master_seed: int = 0xC12_5EED\n    # ^ slicing-tree has tie-break rng for room ordering when scores tie\n\n    # \u2500\u2500 replay \u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\n    expected_environment_fingerprint_strict: bool = True\n```\n\n---\n\n## \u00a7 3 \u2014 Behaviour\n\n### Phase 0 \u2014 Input + startup validation\n\n1. Capture `EnvironmentFingerprint` (reusing C11b's pattern; C12 adds its own version anchor `C12_VERSION: Final[str] = \"v0.1\"`).\n2. If `expected_environment_fingerprint` is provided and doesn't match, raise `EnvironmentFingerprintMismatchError`.\n3. For each single-floor input: assert `geometry_materialized is True AND placement_safe is True` per B-C12-MATERIALIZATION-CONTRACT. If `requires_transform_resolution is True` (Tier A SHALLOW input), invoke the **transform resolver** sub-step first (\u00a7 3.0a below) to materialize the pending geometry; then re-assert flags.\n\n### Phase 0a \u2014 Transform resolver (Tier A SHALLOW inputs)\n\nA C11b output with `capability_mode == \"PREDICATE_ONLY\"` carries a refined parameter vector but no materialized geometry. The transform resolver is the bridge: it takes the predicate verdict (which mutation operator the candidate represents) plus the refined dimensions and produces a candidate with `geometry_materialized = True`.\n\n**At v0.1, the resolver is a stub** that simply marks the candidate as materialized without doing real geometric transformation. Real per-operator resolvers are filed as `B-C12-TIER-A-RESOLVERS` (per-operator implementations for M1\u2013M5, M9a\u2013d). This stub is sufficient for v1 ship if all SFP inputs are Tier B or M0 (already materialized).\n\n### Phase 1 \u2014 Single-floor placement (SFP) per candidate\n\nFor each `RefinedCandidate` in `single_floor_inputs`:\n\n1. Resolve transforms if needed (Phase 0a).\n2. Build the room-list from `refined_parameters.room_dimensions`.\n3. Pull adjacency hints from `floor_room_brief` (e.g., kitchen-adjacent-to-dining).\n4. Invoke `placement_algorithm` (default: slicing-tree partition; see \u00a7 3.1).\n5. On algorithm success: emit `PlacedCandidate` with placed rooms + computed `shared_edges`.\n6. On algorithm failure under `enforcement_mode=STRICT`: raise `GeometricInfeasibilityError`.\n7. On failure under `WARN`: record a `FailureRecord` and continue.\n\n### Phase 2 \u2014 Multi-floor refinement absorption (MFRA)\n\nFor each `MultiFloorWetZonePlannedCandidate` in `multi_floor_inputs`:\n\n1. Decompose into per-floor sub-candidates.\n2. Run Phase 1 (SFP) on each floor independently.\n3. Run Phase 3 (VAV) on the resulting tuple of `PlacedCandidate`s.\n4. If VAV fails AND iteration count < `multi_floor_max_realign_iterations`: feed alignment-delta back as constraint hints, retry SFP on misaligned floors with column-position constraints, re-run VAV.\n5. On convergence: emit `MultiFloorPlacedCandidate`.\n6. On exhaustion: raise `VerticalAlignmentError` (STRICT) or record (WARN).\n\n### Phase 3 \u2014 Vertical alignment verification (VAV)\n\nGiven a tuple of `PlacedCandidate`s, one per floor:\n\n1. Identify alignment-relevant features per floor:\n   - Structural columns (from C7 Grid)\n   - Wet-zone stack centroids (from C10 wet-zone metadata)\n   - Staircase landing/run rectangles (currently from FloorRoomBrief; long-term backlog: dedicated stair planner)\n2. For each feature, compute the per-floor `(x_m, y_m)` position.\n3. For each adjacent floor pair `(N, N+1)`: compute deltas; flag any feature whose delta exceeds `vertical_alignment_tolerance_m`.\n4. Build `VerticalAlignmentReport`. If all three alignment categories pass, emit success; else record deltas for the MFRA retry loop.\n\n### Phase 4 \u2014 Provenance assembly\n\nMirrors C11b \u00a7 3 Phase 3:\n\n- Capture env fingerprint + master_seed + algorithm used per candidate\n- Per-candidate telemetry: wallclock time, retry count, algorithm path\n- Structured failure records (B-C11B-FAILURE-SCHEMA-V2 form \u2014 adopted from day one in C12)\n\n---\n\n## \u00a7 3.1 \u2014 Slicing k-d-tree placement algorithm (v1 default)\n\nPer Knecht & K\u00f6nig 2010, the slicing-tree approach to residential floor plans:\n\n1. Sort rooms by area, descending.\n2. Recursively bisect the envelope along the longer dimension.\n3. At each cut, place the largest remaining room aligned to the cut, with shorter-dim against the envelope wall.\n4. If the room doesn't fit the bisected region, backtrack to a different cut orientation.\n5. Repeat until all rooms placed or backtrack limit exhausted.\n\nThis is O(n log n) typical and O(n!) worst-case (full backtrack). For n \u2264 15 rooms (typical Indian residential) the worst case is tractable. Adjacency hints from C8 promote/demote candidate placements but don't override the area-first heuristic at v1.\n\n**Algorithm correctness at v1**: deterministic given `master_seed` (used only for tie-break on equal-area rooms), produces a valid placement OR fails cleanly. Does NOT guarantee optimality.\n\n---\n\n## \u00a7 4 \u2014 Invariants (v0.1 \u2014 will grow during walks)\n\n| # | Invariant | Mode |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Every `PlacedRoom` is fully contained within `(0, 0)` to `(envelope_width_m, envelope_depth_m)`. | RAISE |\n| 2 | No two `PlacedRoom`s on the same floor have overlapping interiors (shared edges allowed). | RAISE |\n| 3 | `PlacedRoom.width_m == RefinedParameters.room_dimensions[i].width_m` for the corresponding room_id (geometry preserves refinement). Tolerance: `0.0` at v1 in `strict` mode; \u22645% deviation allowed under `lenient_shrink`. | RAISE (STRICT) |\n| 4 | Capability-flag consistency at input: `geometry_materialized AND placement_safe` MUST be True (per B-C12-MATERIALIZATION-CONTRACT). | RAISE |\n| 5 | For multi-floor outputs: every alignment-relevant feature aligns within `vertical_alignment_tolerance_m` across adjacent floors. | RAISE |\n| 6 | `floor_index` is monotonically non-decreasing across the `per_floor` tuple in a `MultiFloorPlacedCandidate`. | RAISE |\n| 7 | Deterministic output: same input + same config + same env fingerprint \u2192 byte-equal `PlacedCandidate` tuple. | RAISE (replay tier) |\n| 8 | Every `PlacedCandidate.source_refined_candidate_signature` matches the input `RefinedCandidate.source_topology_candidate_signature` (one-to-one provenance trace). | RAISE |\n| 9 | `placement_algorithm_used` field is populated and matches one of the literal values in `PlacementConfig.placement_algorithm`. | RAISE |\n| 10 | `shared_edges` is computed deterministically from `placed_rooms` (function of geometry, not algorithm state). | RAISE |\n\n---\n\n## \u00a7 5 \u2014 Failure modes (v0.1 \u2014 will grow)\n\n```\nPlacementError (base)\n\u251c\u2500\u2500 PerCandidatePlacementError\n\u2502   \u251c\u2500\u2500 GeometricInfeasibilityError    (no valid placement; STRICT mode)\n\u2502   \u251c\u2500\u2500 CapabilityFlagInconsistencyError  (Inv 4 violation)\n\u2502   \u251c\u2500\u2500 PlacementAlgorithmTimeoutError (per-candidate budget exceeded)\n\u2502   \u2514\u2500\u2500 TransformResolverError         (Tier A stub failure)\n\u251c\u2500\u2500 PerMultiFloorPlacementError\n\u2502   \u251c\u2500\u2500 VerticalAlignmentError         (VAV failed; MFRA retries exhausted)\n\u2502   \u2514\u2500\u2500 MultiFloorDecompositionError   (per-floor input malformed)\n\u251c\u2500\u2500 BatchAllPlacementsFailedError      (WARN mode: every input failed)\n\u251c\u2500\u2500 EnvironmentFingerprintMismatchError (replay tier)\n\u2514\u2500\u2500 InvariantViolationError            (systemic)\n```\n\n---\n\n## \u00a7 6 \u2014 Test coverage targets (v0.1)\n\n- ~30 SFP-only tests: small-envelope placement, large-envelope placement, adjacency-hint honoring, backtrack-on-infeasible, area-sort tie-break determinism, lenient_shrink mode.\n- ~20 VAV tests: column-aligned passing, column-misaligned failing, wet-stack alignment, staircase alignment, mixed-feature alignment.\n- ~25 MFRA tests: 2-floor convergence after 1 retry, 2-floor exhaustion after max-retries, 3-floor cascade, repair-mode behaviour.\n- ~15 orchestrator tests: STRICT/WARN escalation, env fingerprint replay, batch-all-failed, structured failure records.\n- ~10 invariant tests: Inv 1-10 each with positive and negative cases.\n\nTarget ~100 tests at v1 LOCK (mirrors C11a v0.1 scope before its walks expanded coverage).\n\n---\n\n## \u00a7 7 \u2014 Open questions at v0.1 (resolve during Walks #2-#N)\n\n- **Q-1 (HIGH)**: Placement algorithm choice. Slicing k-d-tree (v1 default) is fast but suboptimal. Should v1 ship with CSP-backtrack fallback enabled by default, or only as opt-in? Literature suggests CSP (Regateiro et al. 2012) handles non-rectangular envelopes better.\n- **Q-2 (MEDIUM)**: Vertical alignment tolerance default. `0.0` is strict; `0.05 m` (50mm) is forgiving. Indian construction tolerances are typically \u00b110mm at the slab level. Reviewer-likely critique: 0.0 is unachievable in practice; 0.05 is the right v1 default.\n- **Q-3 (MEDIUM)**: Multi-floor refinement loop bound. `3` retries is a starting point. Should this scale with floor count, or stay flat?\n- **Q-4 (LOW)**: Determinism via `master_seed`. Slicing tree is deterministic without rng; only tie-break uses it. Is `master_seed` needed at v1 or can we defer it to a parallel-execution Q?\n- **Q-5 (HIGH)**: Adjacency hints from C8. At v1 they're soft (promote/demote candidate placements). Should they ever be HARD? E.g., bathroom-must-be-adjacent-to-bedroom is a hard architectural constraint in some cultures. **Q-5 risks scope-creep into KB rules \u2014 guard against.**\n- **Q-6 (MEDIUM)**: Non-rectangular envelopes (L-shaped plots, corner plots). At v0.1 we assume rectangular; real Indian residential plots are often irregular. Probably backlog for v2.\n- **Q-7 (LOW)**: Handoff contract to C13. `shared_edges` should be sufficient; verify with C13 spec stub.\n- **Q-8 (MEDIUM)**: Performance budget. `10s per single-floor candidate` is generous; `30s for multi-floor with retries` is conservative. Verify against Indian residential pop sizes (typical: 10-15 rooms per floor).\n- **Q-9 (HIGH)**: Repair mode under input infeasibility. STRICT vs LENIENT_SHRINK. The LENIENT mode is dangerous \u2014 it silently changes C11b's refined output, breaking the C11b \u2192 C12 contract that \"C11b chooses dims; C12 places them.\" If we offer it, must we also emit a `repair_delta` provenance field?\n- **Q-10 (MEDIUM)**: Cache key. Does C12 have its own cache (extending C11b's env tuple), or does C12 piggyback C11b's cache by treating placement as deterministic given the input candidate signature?\n- **Q-11 (LOW)**: Multi-floor refinement re-running C11b. Should MFRA re-invoke C11b NSGA-II per floor (the v1.1 LOCKED `B-C11B-MF` deferral path), or just run SFP-per-floor with no re-refinement? v0.1 assumes the latter (simpler); reviewer may push for the former.\n- **Q-12 (LOW)**: Capability-flag handling for `M8_MULTI_FLOOR` operator class. At C11b v1.1, M8 is rejected. If C12 absorbs MF inputs that came from M8 mutations, do we re-classify them as `M0_BASE` for downstream consumers, or keep the M8 lineage in provenance?\n\n**12 open questions at v0.1.** All resolvable through Walks #2-#N before LOCK.\n\n---\n\n## \u00a7 8 \u2014 Backlog at v0.1 (Rule 9 enumeration \u2014 to be expanded each walk)\n\n| ID | Description | Origin | Trigger | Effort |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| **B-C12-TIER-A-RESOLVERS** | Per-operator transform resolvers for M1\u2013M5, M9a\u2013d that turn predicate-only Tier A SHALLOW C11b outputs into materialized geometry. Currently \u00a7 3.0a is a stub. | C12 v0.1 \u00a7 3.0a | Before C13 ships; OR when first non-Tier-B candidate reaches C12 | M |\n| **B-C12-CSP-PLACEMENT** | Full CSP-backtrack placement algorithm per Regateiro et al. 2012 block-algebra + O(n\u00b2) incremental path-consistency. If any Tier A SHALLOW C11b output reaches v1 C12, the stub will mark it materialized without doing real geometric transformation \u2014 downstream (C13, C14) will see invalid geometry attributed to a \"materialized\" flag. Mitigation: backlog item `B-C12-TIER-A-RESOLVERS` filed; v1 should ship with a HARD assertion that input `capability_mode == \"MATERIALIZED\"` (Tier B + M0 only) and fail-fast on Tier A until the resolvers are built. Documented as Q-1-alt for Walk #2.\n\n2. **\u00a7 3 Phase 2 (MFRA) iteration loop is hand-wavy.** \"Feed alignment-delta back as constraint hints\" \u2014 the actual mechanism for translating a 50mm misalignment delta into a constrained re-placement is not specified. Risk: at LOCK we discover the loop never converges in practice. Mitigation: Walk #2 must specify the constraint-injection mechanism formally.\n\n3. **Inv 7 (deterministic output) is asserted but the proof is thin.** Slicing-tree is deterministic given input ordering; tie-break uses `master_seed`. But adjacency-hint scoring (Phase 1 step 3) may pull from `floor_room_brief` in an order-dependent way. Walk #2 must verify the hint-lookup is canonical.\n\n4. **No interaction with B-C11B-PROVENANCE-SPLIT yet.** C11b's `LocalRefinementProvenance` is about to split into three dataclasses. C12's `PlacementProvenance` should anticipate the same shape (replay / operational / diagnostic separation) rather than carry a monolithic block forward.\n\n5. **Capability-flag check timing.** \u00a7 3 Phase 0 step 3 asserts flags before placement. Good. But what about RefinedCandidates that successfully passed C11b's `__post_init__` W6-1 hard check yet were tampered with in-flight? At v1 we trust the singleton path; at v2 we may need a re-check at C12 ingress.\n\n**Self-analysis: no functional bugs.** The spec is internally consistent for v0.1 PROPOSED scope. Issues #1-#5 are walk-resolvable, not LOCK-blockers.\n\n**Web research verification:**\n\n- Searched \"architectural floor plan placement algorithm 2D rectangle packing\" \u2014 confirmed Knecht & K\u00f6nig 2010 slicing-tree approach + Regateiro et al. 2012 CSP block-algebra. Both filed.\n- Floor-planning NP-hardness confirmed per Klawitter et al. 2021 (arxiv 2107.05036). v1's algorithm choice (heuristic slicing + backtrack) is the standard pragmatic compromise.\n\n---\n\n## \u00a7 10 \u2014 Status\n\n**v0.1 PROPOSED.** PENDING Ramalingam LOCK adjudication.\n\n**Open items**: 12 Q-questions in \u00a7 7 + 5 self-audit concerns in \u00a7 9.\n\n**Walks remaining**: at least 2-3 before LOCK candidacy (analogous to C11a's path from v0.1 \u2192 v1.0 over 4 walks).\n\n**Next session (S44+)** action item: Walk #2 review of v0.1 PROPOSED, focused on Q-1, Q-5, Q-9 (the three HIGH-priority open questions) plus self-audit issue #1 (Tier A resolver stub).\n\n---\n\n## \u00a7 11 \u2014 Glossary deltas (terminology adopted from C11b)\n\n- **`EnvironmentFingerprint`**: same shape as C11b's (env tuple + version anchors). C12 adds `c12_version: str` field. Re-uses C11b's `master_seed` capture pattern.\n- **`capability_mode`**: read from `RefinedCandidate` per C11b \u00a7 0.3.1. \"MATERIALIZED\" is required at C12 ingress.\n- **WARN / STRICT enforcement**: same semantics as C11b \u00a7 0.4.\n\n---\n\n## \u00a7 12 \u2014 Backlog visibility inside spec (Rule 9 summary table)\n\n| ID | Description | Origin | Trigger | Effort
